rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every pronoun/demonstrative resolves inside its own chunk or against a term the same file already named earlier (chunk 2 line 23 "Worktrees are the middle path" reuses "Worktrees", named chunk 1 line 13; chunk 4 line 56 "the bug-fix session"/"the feature session" reuse the worktree names from chunk 3's numbered list, lines 39-41). rules_evaluated.evidence: Every chunk (1-7) carries multiple paragraphs or a numbered/bulleted list with self-carrying claims; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

chunk 4 "Stashing and switching between sessions": line 68: "Agent committed to the wrong branch in one session? Don't tie your brain in knots. `git reset --soft HEAD~1` keeps the changes staged, switch branches, re-commit on the right one." — a wrong-branch git-reset recovery tip that isn't stashing or switching between sessions; the header doesn't literally summarize this closing beat of the chunk.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Give the wrong-branch fix its own short aside, or widen the header to cover session/branch recovery generally.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidates: chunk 3 line 44 "Each session has its own scrollback, its own working directory, its own branch" and chunk 2 line 29 "Two folders, two branches, zero checkout churn" are anaphoric triples, but each leg names a genuinely distinct concrete noun (scrollback / working directory / branch; folders / branches / churn) rather than an empty repeat, so they stay inside the "third leg carries new concrete content" exception. No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction, no self-grading superlative, no number-then-retraction, no abstraction-noun stack found in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 "When NOT to run multi-session": line 86: "3. **You are new to the loop.** If you are still learning what \"good\" looks like in one session, adding a second session adds variables, not learning." — this file is a reference/lookup page so the per-slide bold-count budget is waived for its list-shaped sections (chunk 2's "**Branches**/**Clones**/**Worktrees**" and chunk 6's own siblings "**Ordering dependencies.**"/"**Greedy parallelism on a small task.**" are fine under that waiver), but the handle cap still binds. Item 3 bolds a full subject+verb clause ("You are new to the loop") rather than a noun-phrase label, unlike its two list siblings.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast to a noun-phrase handle matching the other two items, e.g. "**New to the loop.**"
